title: Deep learning-guided high-throughput screening and molecular dynamics simulations facilitate the discovery of potential FXIIa inhibitors.
authors: Cai, Fengze; Chen, Wanjun; Xie, Song; Wu, Juhong; Zhang, Yongqi; Gao, Ping; Zhang, Han; Li, Jinyu
one_liner_zh: 该文利用深度学习虚拟筛选和分子动力学模拟发现FXIIa抑制剂，虽以药物发现为目标，但核心方法涉及蛋白结构柔性采样和对接，对蛋白质结构计算有参考价值。
abstract: CONTEXT: Pathological thrombosis is a major cause of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. Current anticoagulants increase bleeding risk by impairing physiological hemostasis. Because coagulation factor XIIa (FXIIa) drives pathological thrombosis but is dispensable for normal hemostasis, inhibiting FXIIa may offer antithrombotic efficacy with reduced bleeding risk. However, the marked flexibility of its active site hampers the discovery of small-molecule inhibitors. Here, we developed an integrated computational workflow to address this challenge and screened a library of approximately 21 million compounds. Four structurally distinct hits (DR1-DR4) were identified. Microsecond-scale molecular dynamics simulations suggested stable binding of all four compounds to FXIIa, and binding free energy calculations suggested that DR1 and DR3 exhibited more favorable binding free energies than the reference inhibitor 1303. These compounds also showed favorable predicted pharmacokinetic properties, providing structurally distinct hits for FXIIa-targeted anticoagulant discovery. METHODS: The crystal structure of the FXIIa catalytic domain (PDB ID: 6B74) was prepared in PyMOL 3.1, and missing regions were modeled with MODELLER. To capture active-site flexibility, apo-FXIIa was subjected to three independent 1-micros molecular dynamics simulations, and a representative conformation selected by clustering was used for virtual screening. A hierarchical screening workflow was carried out in DrugFlow using KarmaDock for primary screening, CarsiDock for redocking, and RTMScore for rescoring. Drug-likeness and pharmacokinetic properties were predicted with SwissADME. Selected complexes were simulated in Amber18 using ff19SB for the protein, GAFF2 for ligands, OPC water, and AM1-BCC ligand charges, and trajectories were analyzed with CPPTRAJ in AmberTools. Binding free energies were estimated with MMPBSA.py using the MM/GBSA method, with entropy contributions evaluated by normal mode analysis. Structural visualization was performed with PyMOL and Discovery Studio Visualizer 2016.
abstract_zh:
背景：病理性血栓形成是心脑血管疾病的主要原因。现有抗凝药物通过损害生理性止血而增加出血风险。由于凝血因子XIIa（FXIIa）驱动病理性血栓形成，但对正常止血并非必需，抑制FXIIa可能提供抗血栓疗效并降低出血风险。然而，其活性位点的显著柔性阻碍了小分子抑制剂的发现。在此，我们开发了一种整合的计算工作流程以应对这一挑战，并筛选了约2100万种化合物的文库。鉴定出四种结构不同的先导化合物（DR1-DR4）。微秒级分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟表明所有四种化合物与FXIIa稳定结合，结合自由能计算表明DR1和DR3表现出比参考抑制剂1303更有利的结合自由能。这些化合物还显示出良好的预测药代动力学特性，为靶向FXIIa的抗凝药物发现提供了结构多样的先导化合物。

方法：FXIIa催化结构域的晶体结构（PDB ID: 6B74）在PyMOL 3.1中制备，缺失区域使用MODELLER建模。为捕捉活性位点柔性，对无配体FXIIa进行了三次独立的1微秒分子动力学模拟，并通过聚类选择的代表性构象用于虚拟筛选。在DrugFlow中采用分层筛选工作流程，使用KarmaDock进行初筛，CarsiDock进行重对接，RTMScore进行重新评分。药物相似性和药代动力学特性使用SwissADME预测。选定的复合物在Amber18中使用ff19SB（蛋白质）、GAFF2（配体）、OPC水模型和AM1-BCC配体电荷进行模拟，轨迹使用AmberTools中的CPPTRAJ分析。结合自由能使用MMPBSA.py通过MM/GBSA方法估算，熵贡献通过简正模式分析评估。结构可视化使用PyMOL和Discovery Studio Visualizer 2016进行。
